title: bug: local-runner.test.mjs A1 fails under Windows node.exe (admission refuses a non-executable git path with the checkout-root error)
description:
Found by worker-fe18a9a9 while verifying task-2cf1c6be. It predates that task: the same result appears on eea1bcaf~1.

Repro: `node.exe --test <D: copy>\scripts\tests\local-runner.test.mjs` with Windows Node v24.16.0. A1 fails on the `{git: <the test file itself>}` row. It expects admission's invalid-input refusal, but gets Error 'Candidate admission repository was not a supported checkout root.' On Linux A1 passes.

Next step: decide whether admitCandidate checks the git executable after the checkout-root probe on win32 (a product ordering gap), or whether the row's non-executable-file premise does not hold on Windows (a test portability gap that needs a skip).

implementationPlan.description:
Decision (the task asked for one): this is a test portability gap, not a product ordering gap. No skip is needed and admission.mjs does not change.
- The failing row is A1's `{ git: path.relative(process.cwd(), fileURLToPath(import.meta.url)) }`.
- On Windows, path.relative from a cwd on another root (another drive, or a \\wsl.localhost UNC share when node.exe is launched from WSL /tmp) returns an ABSOLUTE 'D:\...\local-runner.test.mjs'.
- readInput then accepts it, since it is absolute, exists and lies outside the scratch repo. openRepository's first Git call (rev-parse --show-toplevel) fails on a non-git file and maps to ADMISSION_REPOSITORY_UNSUPPORTED.
- Admission never checks executability on any OS. An absolute non-git file reaches openRepository on Linux too, and Windows has no exec bit to check. So nothing in the product needs reordering.
- Proven at c7493fb2 with Windows node v24.16.0 on a clean archive of HEAD. A1 passes with the cwd on the file's own root. It fails with 'Candidate admission repository was not a supported checkout root.' from C:\Windows\Temp or D:\projexts.
RED first, before editing, take a pristine snapshot and confirm `not ok N - A1` plus that message:
`SNAP=$(mktemp -d /tmp/moe-b294-red.XXXXXX); git archive HEAD | tar -x -C "$SNAP"; (cd /mnt/c/Windows/Temp && "/mnt/c/Program Files/nodejs/node.exe" --test-reporter=tap "$(wslpath -w "$SNAP/scripts/tests/local-runner.test.mjs")") | grep -aE '^(not )?ok [0-9]+ - A1 |supported checkout root'`
Run the file directly. `node.exe --test <UNC path>` fails with "Could not find" (glob).
Fix, in scripts/tests/local-runner.test.mjs A1 only. In the A1 body, before `const base` and therefore before `changes` computes path.relative, add a 3-line comment saying why: Windows path.relative across drive or UNC roots is absolute, so the relative-git row became an absolute non-git file that admission ran. Then add:
```js
const cwd = process.cwd();
t.after(() => process.chdir(cwd));
process.chdir(path.dirname(fileURLToPath(import.meta.url)));
```
This is the established pattern in scripts/tests/local-runner-vm-control.test.mjs:279-280 and local-runner-snapshot.test.mjs:418. The row then reads 'local-runner.test.mjs' on every OS and cwd, and it still resolves to an existing file outside the repo. That keeps its mutation power: in scratch, a readInput mutant dropping `path.isAbsolute(git)` fails A1 on that row.
Keep the row expression, the 'relative git the cwd resolves' comment and every other row unchanged. Error handling: the chdir target is the test file's own existing directory, not a temp dir, so the scratch dirs' t.after rm is never blocked on Windows. t.after restores the cwd even when A1 fails.
implementationPlan.note: Added saved cwd, t.after restore, chdir to test file dir + 3-line comment in A1. Shared tree has 35 other dirty paths, untouched. RED reproduction deferred to the gate (pristine snapshot run alongside).

planningNotes.approachesConsidered:
(1) Product change: check executability or ordering in admitCandidate. Rejected: admission never checks the exec bit on any OS, Windows has none, and an absolute non-git file gives REPOSITORY_UNSUPPORTED on Linux too, so the product is consistent.
(2) Skip the row on win32. Rejected: CI's Windows runner (same-drive cwd) passes it, and a skip would drop coverage that is easy to keep.
(3) Fall back to a bare relative name when path.relative is absolute. Rejected: the value would no longer resolve from the cwd, which weakens the row's mutation power on Windows.
(4) Chosen: chdir into the test file's directory for A1, then restore it. The row stays relative and resolvable on every OS.
Prototype at c7493fb2:
- Windows A1 passes from the snapshot, C: and D: cwds.
- Linux A1 passes.
- Mutant without path.isAbsolute(git): A1 fails.
- Full file: Windows 215 pass, 41 skip, only AJ3-6 fail; Linux 255 pass, only AJ3-6 fail. AJ3-6 fail identically at pristine HEAD.
